title: Run a Fair Test With Your Child

scenes.tts: Does a plant really need sunlight if it already has water? Ask your child for a guess. A fair test is a test where only one thing changes and everything else stays the same. Four cups of radish seedlings can show you how.
scenes.visual: A cup with a sprout, a sun with a question mark, and a water drop; a guess chip; two identical cups where only one thing changes; becomes four cups in a row.
scenes.narration: Does a plant really need sunlight if it already has water? Ask your child for a guess. A fair test is a test where only one thing changes and everything else stays the same. Four cups of radish seedlings can show you how.

scenes.tts: First, grow all four cups the same way. Same soil, same cups, same seeds, all on a sunny windowsill. Wait until most seedlings are about two centimetres tall. Before you change anything, ask your child what will happen to each cup. Write or draw the guesses. The safety notes are on the page.
scenes.visual: Four identical cups with equal sprouts on a windowsill under a sun; sameness ticks; question marks and a guess sheet appear over each cup.
scenes.narration: First, grow all four cups the same way. Same soil, same cups, same seeds, all on a sunny windowsill. Wait until most seedlings are about two centimetres tall. Before you change anything, ask your child what will happen to each cup. Write or draw the guesses. The safety notes are on the page.

scenes.tts: Now change things. Move two cups into the cupboard, where it is dark. Two cups keep their water. Two get nothing more. Change nothing else. Next to the light and water cup, the dark and water cup differs only in light. The light, no water cup differs only in water.
scenes.visual: Two cups slide into a cupboard; drops over two cups, none over the others; gold rings show the single difference against the light and water cup.
scenes.narration: Now change things. Move two cups into the cupboard, where it is dark. Two cups keep their water. Two get nothing more. Change nothing else. Next to the light and water cup, the dark and water cup differs only in light. The light, no water cup differs only in water.

scenes.tts: Now look and compare. Check every day or two, and draw each cup. The cups with no water usually droop within two to five days. Within about a week, the watered seedlings in the dark are often taller, thinner and paler. The cup with light and water stays green and upright.
scenes.visual: Time passes; dry cups droop; the dark watered sprout stretches tall, thin and pale; the light and water sprout stays short, sturdy, green.
scenes.narration: Now look and compare. Check every day or two, and draw each cup. The cups with no water usually droop within two to five days. Within about a week, the watered seedlings in the dark are often taller, thinner and paler. The cup with light and water stays green and upright.

scenes.tts: Look again at the dark seedlings. They are the tallest. Your child may call them the best. So ask about colour and strength, not only height. A seedling in the dark stretches on food it has stored. Once that food runs out, it grows weaker. Height alone is not health. If a result surprises your child, it is still real, so do not throw it out.
scenes.visual: The tall pale sprout gets a height bar and a question; colour and strength checks appear; stored-food bar empties; the result chip stays.

scenes.tts: If your child wants extra water for one cup, do not change that cup. Add an extra cup to try the idea, and the first test stays fair. Here is the short version. Predict first. Change one thing at a time. Keep everything else the same. Look and compare. Keep every real result.
scenes.visual: A new extra cup joins at the side; five rule lines appear one by one beside the four cups.
